elements.title: hash(key) → ring position
elements.subtitle: Consistent-hash placement
elements.body:
FIND THE OWNER
  Start at hash(key) · move clockwise
  First token: vB2 → Cache Shard B

metadata.explanation:
Clockwise-successor stopping rule
hash(key) → first virtual-node token clockwise
1. hash(key) produces one position on the ring.
2. Starting at that position, move clockwise.
3. Stop at the first virtual-node token encountered.
4. In this example, that token is vB2.
5. The key range ending at vB2 maps to logical Cache Shard B.
6. Shard B’s replica-selection rule then chooses physical server B1, B2, or B3.

vB2 owns the ring interval after its predecessor and up to vB2.

elements.title: Cache quorum
elements.subtitle: N=3 · R=2 · W=2
elements.body:
OVERLAPPING QUORUMS
  3 copies · read 2 · await 2 write replies
  R + W > N · tolerates one failed server

WORK PER REQUEST
  Read: 2 operations · write / refill: 3

COMBINED CHOSEN BUDGET
  3 × 50,000 = 150,000 node operations/s
  Read-only limit: 75,000 client requests/s

metadata.explanation:
Cache quorum + availability
N=3 · R=2 · W=2
N=3: three physical servers per shard.
R=2: read two versioned values; return the newest.
W=2: require two cache write acknowledgements.
R+W>N: the read and write quorums intersect.
ONE SERVER DOWN: two healthy replicas still form a quorum.
FEWER THAN TWO: do not serve a single potentially stale copy.
metadata.outputs: newest version or quorum failure

elements.title: Acknowledged write
elements.subtitle: Synchronous write-through
elements.body:
BOTH MUST SUCCEED
  Cache W=2 + Cassandra CL=QUORUM

CLIENT SUCCESS
  Acknowledge only after both quorums

metadata.explanation:
Acknowledged-write rule
cache W=2 + Cassandra CL=QUORUM
A financial write is acknowledged only after both required quorums succeed for the same version. If either side fails, do not acknowledge; invalidate or bypass the cache until Cassandra refreshes it.
metadata.inputs: cache W=2 acknowledgements and Cassandra CL=QUORUM acknowledgement
metadata.outputs: client success or explicit failure plus cache invalidation

elements.title: Memory policy
elements.subtitle: LFU eviction · TTL expiry
elements.body:
REMOVE ENTRIES
  LFU: least frequently used
  TTL: expired entries

NEXT READ
  Miss → Cassandra → refill

metadata.explanation: LFU eviction removes the least frequently used entries; TTL expiry removes aged entries. Both produce a MISS, followed by an authoritative Cassandra read and cache refill.

elements.title: Hot-key options
elements.subtitle: Application load protection
elements.body:
REDUCE REPEATED WORK
  Coalesce misses for the same key
  Spread reads across healthy replicas

KEEP CONSISTENCY
  R=2 / W=2 · no stale single-copy fallback

metadata.inputs: concentrated requests for one financial key
metadata.outputs: coalesced authoritative reads or reads spread across the existing replica set
metadata.explanation: These are load-protection options, not a change to the selected topology. Single-flight database fallback can combine concurrent cache misses. Reads remain versioned R=2 quorums; writes still require cache W=2 plus Cassandra CL=QUORUM. Increasing the replica factor requires reevaluating N, R and W before adoption.

elements.title: Cassandra
elements.subtitle: Authoritative source of truth
elements.body:
REPLICATION + QUORUM
  RF=3: three durable copies
  CL=QUORUM: two of three must respond

PARTITION KEY
  user_id chooses the database partition

metadata.explanation:
Cassandra cluster
authoritative · RF=3 · CL=QUORUM · partition key=user_id
RF=3: Cassandra stores 3 durable copies of each row.
CL=QUORUM: 2 of 3 database replicas must respond to the read or write.
PARTITION KEY: user_id chooses the database partition.
metadata.inputs: miss reads and synchronous financial writes
metadata.outputs: quorum result and durable versioned rows

metadata.outputs: Load, spare capacity and first limit
metadata.explanation:
Budget
3 hosts × 5,000 operations/s = 15,000 total (assumed).

Peak work
Writes: 2,000 × 3 copies = 6,000 ops/s.
Reads: 200 cache misses × 2 copies = 400 ops/s.
Total: 6,400 ops/s · 43% used.

Consequence
2× traffic uses 85%: below the 50% spare-capacity target.
Cassandra reaches its budget first at ≈9,400 client requests/s.
